title: Static and kinetic friction
target: Distinguish adjustable static friction from sliding friction.
criteria: Compare a push with the static-friction limit.
Find actual friction for rest or sliding.
Explain friction direction using relative slipping.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Maximum static friction is 24 N. A horizontal 15 N push leaves a box at rest with no other horizontal forces. What is actual friction?
options: 0 N because the box is stationary.
cpa.guide: Static friction adjusts to balance the push up to its limit.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A resting box has a 24 N static-friction limit. The horizontal push rises to 30 N with no other horizontal forces. What does the model predict?
options: Static friction automatically becomes 30 N despite its limit.
Static friction cannot hold it at rest.
It must remain at rest because friction exists.
Its normal force must become zero.
cpa.guide: The required balancing friction exceeds the maximum.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A box slides right under a 30 N rightward push and 18 N kinetic friction. What is net force?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A sliding object has μ_k = 0.25 and normal force 40 N. What is kinetic-friction magnitude?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A box slides right relative to a stationary floor. Which way does floor friction act on the box?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A moving conveyor belt carries a box without slipping and accelerates it to the right. Can static friction on the box point right?
options: No; friction always points opposite motion relative to the room.
No; static friction is always zero.
Yes; it can prevent relative slipping and accelerate the box with the belt.
Yes; but only if the box has negative mass.
cpa.guide: Friction concerns relative motion or its tendency at contact, not a universal opposition to room-frame velocity.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
